messages.content: What does a GPU do well?
It runs many threads in parallel, which suits matrix multiplication.
Storing weights with fewer bits and rescaling them when they are used.
It keeps earlier keys and values so they are not recomputed for each new token.
A method that freezes the base weights and trains small low rank matrices added to some layers.
Training a small student model to imitate a larger teacher model.
Mostly memory bandwidth, because every weight is read for each generated token.
A saved copy of the weights and optimiser state that lets training resume.
So an experiment can be repeated and compared fairly.
A cheap drafter proposes tokens and the large model verifies them together.
It removes parts of a model, such as heads or channels, to make it smaller.
A store of key value blocks for shared prompt prefixes, reused across requests.
Rounding up or down at random so that the average rounding error is zero.
Adding new requests to a running batch as soon as others finish.
Why evaluate against the parent model?
To see what compression changed, using the same prompts and uncertainty estimates.
A bound on speed set by either memory bandwidth or peak arithmetic throughput.
A small, fast run that touches every stage to show the plumbing works.
A program that maps text to integer token ids and back.
Why warm up the learning rate?
Early updates are noisy, so a gentle start keeps training stable.
Limiting the gradient norm so one bad batch cannot ruin the weights.
Storage where each object is named by the hash of its bytes.
